junior.title: 🌲 Trees That Talk — The Hidden Forest Network
junior.content:
Have you ever walked through a forest and felt that the trees were somehow alive in a special way? 🔬 Scientists have discovered that trees can actually communicate with each other!

Under the ground, trees are connected by a huge network of tiny roots and fungi. This underground network is sometimes called the “Wood Wide Web”. Through this network, trees can share water and nutrients. When a young tree is weak, older trees nearby can send it extra food to help it grow stronger. Isn’t that amazing? 🌳

Trees also send warnings about danger. If insects attack one tree, it can send chemical signals through the air and the roots. Other trees receive the message and start producing special chemicals to protect themselves. In this way, the whole forest works together like a big family.

Why is this important for us? Forests help clean the air we breathe and give us oxygen. They also provide homes for many animals and plants. When we cut down too many trees, we break this beautiful network. That is why it is so important to protect forests and plant more trees.

Next time you walk in a park or a forest, take a moment to look at the trees. Remember that under your feet, they may be quietly talking to each other, sharing food, and helping their neighbours. Nature is full of secrets, and the more we learn, the more we understand how precious our environment is. Let’s all try to take better care of the green world around us! 🌍
junior.translation:
你有没有走过森林，感觉树木以某种特殊的方式活着？🔬 科学家们已经发现，树木其实可以互相交流！

在地下，树木通过由细小根须和真菌组成的巨大网络连接在一起。这个地下网络有时被称为“树木互联网”。通过这个网络，树木可以分享水分和营养。当一棵小树较弱时，附近的大树可以给它额外的食物，帮助它长得更强壮。这是不是很神奇？🌳

树木还会发出危险警告。如果昆虫攻击一棵树，它可以通过空气和根部发出化学信号。其他树木收到信息后，会开始产生特殊的化学物质来保护自己。这样，整片森林就像一个大家庭一样共同协作。

这对我们为什么重要？森林帮助净化我们呼吸的空气，并提供氧气。它们还为许多动植物提供家园。当我们砍伐太多树木时，就会破坏这个美丽的网络。这就是为什么保护森林、多种树如此重要。

下次你在公园或森林里散步时，花点时间看看那些树。记住，在你脚下，它们可能正在悄悄地互相交谈、分享食物、帮助邻居。大自然充满秘密，我们学得越多，就越能理解环境是多么珍贵。让我们都努力更好地照顾身边的绿色世界吧！🌍

junior.title: 🚀 A Day of a Young Astronaut
junior.content:
Have you ever dreamed of becoming an astronaut and flying into space? 🌌 Let’s imagine a day in the life of a young astronaut on a space station.

The day starts early. There is no sunrise or sunset in space the way we see them on Earth, but the astronaut still follows a schedule. First, she checks the systems of the spacecraft to make sure everything is working well. Then she has breakfast. In space, food comes in special packages, and there is no gravity, so drinks and crumbs float around if you are not careful!

After breakfast, the astronaut begins her science experiments. She may study how plants grow without gravity, or how the human body changes in space. These experiments help scientists on Earth understand more about life and prepare for future journeys to the Moon or Mars. 🔬

In the afternoon, she does physical training. Living without gravity makes muscles and bones weaker, so astronauts must exercise every day on special machines. It is hard work, but necessary to stay healthy.

Later, she may look out of the window. From space, the Earth looks beautiful — blue oceans, white clouds, and green land. There are no borders visible. Many astronauts say this view makes them feel how important it is to protect our planet. 🌍

In the evening, she talks with her family on Earth through video calls and writes in her journal. Before sleeping, she looks at the stars and thinks about how far humans have come, and how much more there is still to explore in the universe.

Being an astronaut is full of challenges, but it is also one of the most exciting jobs in the world. Who knows? Maybe one day you will be the one floating among the stars! ✨
junior.translation:
你有没有梦想过成为宇航员，飞向太空？🌌 让我们想象一下一位年轻宇航员在空间站的一天。

一天很早开始。太空中没有我们在地球上看到的那种日出日落，但宇航员仍然遵循作息时间。首先，她检查航天器的系统，确保一切正常。然后吃早餐。在太空中，食物装在特殊包装里，没有重力，所以如果不小心，饮料和碎屑会飘得到处都是！

早餐后，宇航员开始科学实验。她可能研究植物在没有重力的情况下如何生长，或者人体在太空中如何变化。这些实验帮助地球上的科学家更多地了解生命，并为未来前往月球或火星的旅程做准备。🔬

下午，她进行体能训练。没有重力的生活会让肌肉和骨骼变弱，所以宇航员必须每天在特殊机器上锻炼。这很辛苦，但对保持健康很有必要。

晚些时候，她可能会望向窗外。从太空看，地球美丽极了——蓝色的海洋、白色的云朵和绿色的陆地。看不到任何国界。许多宇航员说，这种景色让他们感受到保护我们星球是多么重要。🌍

晚上，她通过视频通话与地球上的家人聊天，并写日记。睡觉前，她望着星星，思考人类已经走了多远，以及宇宙中还有多少值得探索的地方。

成为宇航员充满挑战，但也是世界上最令人兴奋的工作之一。谁知道呢？也许有一天，飘浮在星空中的人就是你！✨

junior.title: 📚 The Magic Power of Reading
junior.content:
Reading is like having a magic key that can open thousands of doors. 📖 With a book in your hand, you can travel to any place in the world, meet interesting people, and experience amazing adventures — all without leaving your chair!

When you read a story, your imagination starts working. You can see the characters in your mind, hear their voices, and feel their feelings. A good book can make you laugh, cry, or think deeply about life. That is the special power of reading.

Reading also helps you learn. Every book is full of new words and ideas. The more you read, the larger your vocabulary becomes, and the better you understand the world. Students who read a lot often find it easier to write good compositions and do well in exams, because they have more knowledge and better language skills.

But reading is not only useful — it is also fun. There are books about animals, space, history, mystery, friendship, and almost everything else you can think of. You can choose what you like and enjoy it at your own speed. Unlike watching videos, reading lets you stop, think, and go back whenever you want.

To become a good reader, you need to build a habit. Try to read for at least fifteen or twenty minutes every day. Find a quiet place, turn off your phone, and dive into the story. At first it may feel a little hard to concentrate, but soon you will find it hard to stop!

Books are treasures that never grow old. The stories your grandparents loved can still touch your heart today. So open a book, and let the magic begin. Who knows what wonderful worlds you will discover next? ✨
junior.translation:
阅读就像拥有一把能打开成千上万扇门的魔法钥匙。📖 手里拿着一本书，你可以去世界任何地方旅行，遇见有趣的人，体验奇妙的冒险——这一切都不需要离开你的椅子！

当你读故事时，你的想象力开始运转。你可以在脑海中看到人物，听到他们的声音，感受他们的情感。一本好书可以让你开怀大笑、流泪，或者深入思考人生。这就是阅读的特殊力量。

阅读还能帮助你学习。每本书都充满新单词和新想法。你读得越多，词汇量就越大，对世界的理解也越好。爱读书的学生往往更容易写出好作文、在考试中取得好成绩，因为他们知识更丰富，语言能力更强。

但阅读不仅有用——它也很有趣。有关于动物、太空、历史、悬疑、友谊的书，几乎你能想到的一切都有。你可以选择自己喜欢的，按照自己的节奏去享受。与看视频不同，阅读可以让你随时停下来思考，或回过头再看。

要成为一名好的读者，你需要养成习惯。试着每天至少读十五到二十分钟。找一个安静的地方，关掉手机，沉浸到故事中。一开始可能有点难集中注意力，但很快你就会发现停不下来！

书是永不老去的宝藏。你祖父母曾经喜欢的故事，今天依然能触动你的心。所以打开一本书，让魔法开始吧。谁知道你接下来会发现怎样精彩的世界呢？✨

junior.title: 🤖 Robots in Our Daily Life
junior.content:
Have you ever seen a robot? Robots are no longer just in science fiction movies. They are becoming part of our daily life. 🤖

In factories, robots work day and night. They can do heavy and dangerous jobs that humans find difficult. For example, they move heavy boxes, paint cars, and even check the quality of products. Because robots never get tired, factories can produce more things in less time.

At home, some families use robots to clean the floor. These robots move around the room automatically and collect dust. Other robots can help cook or water the plants. In hospitals, special robots help doctors perform operations more carefully. In schools, some robots are used to teach children languages or science in a fun way.

Of course, robots still need humans. People invent robots, write the programs that control them, and repair them when something goes wrong. Robots cannot think or feel like humans. They only do what they are programmed to do.

Some people worry that robots will replace human workers and take away jobs. Others believe that robots will create new kinds of jobs and make life more convenient. What do you think? Will robots make our future better? One thing is certain: learning about science and technology will help us understand and use robots wisely. 🚀

在工厂里，机器人日夜工作。它们能做人类觉得困难的重活和危险工作。例如，它们搬运重箱子、给汽车喷漆，甚至检查产品质量。因为机器人永不疲倦，工厂能在更短时间内生产更多东西。

junior.title: ⏰ The Power of Small Daily Habits
junior.content:
Do you want to become better at English, sports, or any skill? The secret is not doing something big once, but doing small things every day. 🌱

Think about learning English. If you only study hard one day before the exam, you may still forget most of the words. But if you learn ten new words every day and review them, after one year you will know more than three thousand words! Small daily efforts create big results.

The same is true for sports. Running for five minutes every day is better than running for one hour only once a month. Your body gets stronger little by little. Reading ten pages of a book every night is better than trying to finish a whole book in one weekend.

Why do small habits work so well? Because they are easy to start and easy to continue. When a task is too big, we often feel tired and give up. When it is small, we can finish it even on busy days. Over time, these small actions become automatic — they become real habits.

To build a good habit, choose something small and clear. For example: “I will read English for ten minutes after dinner.” Write it down and do it every day for at least three weeks. Be patient. Progress may feel slow at first, but one day you will look back and be surprised by how far you have come.

Remember: success is not about sudden big changes. It is about the small things you do every single day. Start today, and let your daily habits shape a better you. ✨
junior.translation:
你想在英语、运动或任何技能上变得更好吗？秘密不是偶尔做一件大事，而是每天做小事情。🌱

想想学英语。如果只在考试前一天努力学习，你可能还是会忘记大部分单词。但如果你每天学十个新词并复习，一年后你就会认识三千多个词！每天的小努力会创造大结果。

运动也是一样。每天跑五分钟，比一个月只跑一次一小时要好。你的身体会一点点变强。每天晚上读十页书，比周末试图读完整本书要好。

为什么小习惯如此有效？因为它们容易开始、容易坚持。当任务太大时，我们常常感到累并放弃。当它很小时，即使在忙碌的日子也能完成。随着时间推移，这些小行动会变得自动化——它们成为真正的习惯。

要养成好习惯，选择一件又小又明确的事。例如：“晚饭后我读十分钟英语。”写下来，连续至少三周每天做。要有耐心。一开始进步可能感觉很慢，但有一天你会回头看，惊讶于自己走了多远。

记住：成功不是关于突然的大改变。它关于你每天做的小事。从今天开始，让每日习惯塑造更好的你。✨

junior.title: 🐝 Why Bees Are Important to Us
junior.content:
When you eat an apple or a tomato, do you ever think about bees? Bees are small, but they play a huge role in our food and environment. 🐝

Bees help plants by carrying pollen from one flower to another. This process is called pollination. Without pollination, many plants cannot produce fruits and seeds. In fact, about one third of the food we eat depends on bees and other pollinators. Apples, strawberries, cucumbers, and many other fruits and vegetables need bees.

Besides food, bees also help keep nature in balance. When plants grow well because of bees, animals that eat those plants also have enough food. Forests, fields, and gardens all benefit from the work of bees.

Sadly, the number of bees is decreasing in many places. One reason is the use of chemicals that kill insects. Another reason is the loss of wild flowers and natural places where bees can live. Climate change also makes life harder for bees.

What can we do to help? We can plant more flowers that bees like. We can avoid using harmful chemicals in our gardens. We can also tell others how important bees are. Even small actions can make a difference.

Next time you see a bee flying around a flower, remember: that little insect is working hard to help feed the world. Protecting bees means protecting our food and our beautiful environment. 🌸
junior.translation:
当你吃苹果或西红柿时，有没有想过蜜蜂？蜜蜂很小，但它们在我们的食物和环境中扮演着巨大角色。🐝

蜜蜂通过把花粉从一朵花带到另一朵花来帮助植物。这个过程叫做授粉。没有授粉，许多植物无法结出果实和种子。事实上，我们吃的大约三分之一的食物依赖蜜蜂和其他授粉者。苹果、草莓、黄瓜以及许多其他水果和蔬菜都需要蜜蜂。

除了食物，蜜蜂还帮助保持自然平衡。当植物因为蜜蜂而生长良好时，以这些植物为食的动物也有足够的食物。森林、田野和花园都受益于蜜蜂的工作。

可悲的是，许多地方蜜蜂的数量在减少。一个原因是使用杀死昆虫的化学物质。另一个原因是蜜蜂可以生活的野花和自然场所的丧失。气候变化也让蜜蜂的生活更艰难。

我们能做什么来帮助？我们可以种植更多蜜蜂喜欢的花。我们可以避免在花园使用有害化学物质。我们也可以告诉别人蜜蜂有多重要。即使是小行动也能带来改变。

下次你看到蜜蜂在花周围飞时，请记住：那个小昆虫正在努力帮助养活世界。保护蜜蜂就是保护我们的食物和美丽的环境。🌸

junior.title: 🌟 Never Give Up — The Story of a Young Inventor
junior.content:
Have you ever tried something and failed? Many great inventors failed many times before they succeeded. One famous example is Thomas Edison, who invented the electric light. He tried thousands of materials before he found the right one. 💡

A modern young inventor named Xiaoming had a similar experience. When he was 14, he wanted to invent a small machine that could clean the air in classrooms. His first design did not work. The second one made too much noise. The third one was too expensive. Many people told him to give up.

But Xiaoming did not stop. He read books, watched science videos, and asked teachers for advice. He improved his design again and again. After two years of hard work, his machine finally worked well. It was quiet, cheap, and effective. His school started using it, and later other schools became interested too.

Xiaoming’s story teaches us an important lesson: failure is not the end. It is part of the journey to success. Every time we fail, we can learn something new. If we continue trying and improving, we may achieve our goals.

So next time you fail a test or lose a game, remember Xiaoming. Don’t give up. Keep learning, keep trying, and keep believing in yourself. Success often comes to those who refuse to quit. 🌟
junior.translation:
你有没有尝试过什么却失败了？许多伟大的发明家在成功之前都失败过很多次。一个著名的例子是发明电灯的托马斯·爱迪生。他尝试了数千种材料才找到合适的。💡

一位叫小明的现代年轻发明家有类似的经历。他14岁时想发明一种可以净化教室空气的小机器。他的第一个设计没有用。第二个噪音太大。第三个太贵。许多人劝他放弃。

但小明没有停止。他读书、看科学视频、向老师请教。他一次又一次改进设计。经过两年努力，他的机器终于运行良好。它安静、便宜、有效。他的学校开始使用，后来其他学校也感兴趣了。

小明的故事告诉我们一个重要道理：失败不是终点。它是通往成功路上的一部分。每次失败，我们都能学到新东西。如果我们继续尝试和改进，就可能实现目标。

所以下次你考试失败或比赛输掉时，想想小明。不要放弃。继续学习、继续尝试、继续相信自己。成功往往属于那些拒绝放弃的人。🌟

junior.title: 📚 The Joy of Reading Paper Books
junior.content:
In the age of phones and tablets, many people read on screens. Digital books are convenient—you can carry hundreds of books in one device. But more and more students are rediscovering the joy of reading paper books. 📖

Why do some people prefer paper? First, paper books are easier on the eyes. Looking at screens for a long time can make eyes tired. With a paper book, you can read longer and feel more comfortable. Second, paper books help you concentrate. There are no messages or videos popping up to distract you. You can fully enter the world of the story.

Paper books also give a special feeling. You can touch the pages, smell the paper, and write notes in the margins. Turning a page feels different from swiping a screen. Many readers say this physical experience makes the story more memorable.

Libraries and bookshops are wonderful places. Walking among shelves of books, choosing one that looks interesting, and sitting down to read—these simple actions bring quiet happiness. Sharing a paper book with a friend is also a warm way to connect.

Of course, digital reading has its advantages. But paper books still have a unique place in our lives. They are treasures of knowledge and imagination that we can hold in our hands. Next time you have free time, try opening a real book. You may fall in love with reading all over again. ✨

为什么有些人更喜欢纸质书？首先，纸质书对眼睛更友好。长时间看屏幕会让眼睛疲劳。用纸质书，你可以读得更久，感觉更舒适。其次，纸质书帮助你集中注意力。没有消息或视频弹出来打扰你。你可以完全进入故事的世界。

纸质书也给人特别的感觉。你可以触摸书页、闻纸张的味道、在空白处写笔记。翻页的感觉不同于滑动屏幕。许多读者说，这种身体体验让故事更难忘。

图书馆和书店是美妙的地方。走在书架之间，挑选一本看起来有趣的书，坐下来阅读——这些简单的行动带来安静的快乐。与朋友分享一本纸质书也是温暖的联系方式。

当然，数字阅读有其优势。但纸质书在我们生活中仍有独特位置。它们是我们可以握在手中的知识和想象力的宝藏。下次有空时，试着打开一本真正的书。你可能会重新爱上阅读。✨

senior.title: 🌊 The Ocean as Earth’s Climate Engine
senior.content:
The ocean covers more than 70 percent of our planet’s surface, yet many people still think of it mainly as a place for swimming or fishing. In reality, the ocean is one of the most powerful climate regulators on Earth. 🔬

Ocean currents, driven by wind, temperature differences and the Earth’s rotation, move huge amounts of heat around the globe. Warm water travels from the equator toward the poles, while cold water returns toward the tropics. This continuous circulation helps keep temperatures in many regions moderate and stable. Without it, some places would be much hotter and others much colder.

The ocean also absorbs a large share of the carbon dioxide that human activities release into the atmosphere. Phytoplankton — tiny plant-like organisms floating near the surface — take in carbon during photosynthesis. When they die, some of that carbon sinks to the deep ocean, where it can remain locked away for centuries. In this way, the ocean acts as a giant carbon sink that slows the pace of global warming.

However, this vital system is under growing pressure. Rising temperatures cause seawater to expand and ice sheets to melt, contributing to sea-level rise. Warmer water holds less oxygen and can harm coral reefs and other marine ecosystems. At the same time, the ocean’s ability to absorb extra carbon is not unlimited; as it takes in more CO₂, the water becomes more acidic, threatening shellfish and the food chains that depend on them.

Understanding these processes is essential if we want to mitigate climate change. Protecting marine ecosystems, reducing greenhouse-gas emissions and supporting sustainable fishing are all part of the solution. The ocean is not just a beautiful blue landscape — it is a dynamic engine that helps keep our planet livable. The more we learn about it, the clearer it becomes that caring for the ocean means caring for ourselves. 🌍
senior.translation:
海洋覆盖了地球表面超过70%的面积，但许多人仍主要把它当作游泳或钓鱼的地方。实际上，海洋是地球上最强大的气候调节器之一。🔬

由风、温度差异和地球自转驱动的洋流，在全球范围内输送着大量热量。温暖的海水从赤道流向两极，而冷水则返回热带。这种持续的循环有助于使许多地区的温度保持温和稳定。如果没有它，有些地方会热得多，另一些地方则冷得多。

海洋还吸收了人类活动释放到大气中的大量二氧化碳。浮游植物——漂浮在表层的微小植物样生物——在光合作用过程中吸收碳。当它们死亡后，部分碳会沉入深海，并可能在那里封存数百年。这样，海洋就像一个巨大的碳汇，减缓了全球变暖的速度。

然而，这个至关重要的系统正承受着越来越大的压力。气温上升导致海水膨胀、冰盖融化，从而加剧海平面上升。温暖的海水含氧量更低，并可能伤害珊瑚礁和其他海洋生态系统。同时，海洋吸收额外碳的能力并非无限；随着它吸收更多二氧化碳，海水会变得更酸，威胁贝类以及依赖它们的食物链。

如果我们想缓解气候变化，理解这些过程至关重要。保护海洋生态系统、减少温室气体排放、支持可持续捕捞，都是解决方案的一部分。海洋不仅仅是美丽的蓝色风景——它是帮助维持我们星球宜居的动力引擎。我们对它了解得越多，就越清楚：关爱海洋就是关爱我们自己。🌍

senior.title: 🧠 How Habits Quietly Shape Our Future
senior.content:
We often think of success as the result of big decisions or sudden inspiration. In truth, much of who we become is shaped by the small, repeated actions we take every day — our habits. 🔄

A habit is a behaviour that has become automatic through repetition. When you first learn to ride a bicycle or type on a keyboard, every movement requires attention. With practice, the brain creates stronger neural pathways, and the action becomes almost effortless. The same process applies to studying, exercising, reading, or even negative patterns like procrastination.

Because habits run largely on autopilot, they can work for us or against us. A student who reviews notes for twenty minutes every evening is quietly building knowledge and confidence. Another student who checks social media first thing every morning may be reinforcing distraction. Over months and years, these tiny differences compound into very different results.

Changing a habit is possible, but it usually requires more than motivation alone. Motivation comes and goes; systems and environment matter more. Making the desired behaviour easier (for example, putting a book on your pillow) and the unwanted behaviour harder (leaving the phone in another room) increases the chance of success. Tracking progress and celebrating small wins also helps reinforce the new pattern.

Perhaps the deepest power of habits lies in identity. When you repeatedly act like a reader, a runner, or a careful thinker, you begin to see yourself that way. The behaviour and the self-image support each other. In this sense, habits do not just change what we do — they gradually transform who we believe we are.

Building good habits is therefore an act of long-term self-respect. It is not about perfection, but about consistent, intentional effort. The person you will be in five years is being shaped by the habits you practise today. Choose them wisely. 🌱
senior.translation:
我们常常认为成功来自大的决定或突然的灵感。实际上，我们成为什么样的人，很大程度上是由每天重复的小行动——我们的习惯——塑造的。🔄

习惯是一种通过重复变得自动化的行为。当你第一次学骑自行车或打字时，每一个动作都需要注意力。通过练习，大脑会建立更强的神经通路，动作几乎变得不费力。同样的过程也适用于学习、锻炼、阅读，甚至像拖延这样的负面模式。

因为习惯很大程度上在“自动驾驶”状态下运行，它们既可以为我们服务，也可能与我们作对。一个每天晚上复习二十分钟笔记的学生，正在悄悄积累知识和自信。另一个每天早上第一件事就刷社交媒体的学生，可能在强化分心。几个月、几年后，这些微小的差异会累积成截然不同的结果。

改变习惯是可能的，但通常需要的不只是动机。动机来了又走；系统和环境更重要。让期望的行为更容易（比如把书放在枕头上），让不想要的行为更难（把手机放在另一个房间），会提高成功的几率。记录进度并庆祝小胜利也有助于强化新模式。

也许习惯最深层的力量在于身份认同。当你反复表现得像一个读者、跑步者或谨慎的思考者时，你开始以这种方式看待自己。行为与自我形象相互支持。从这个意义上说，习惯不仅改变我们做什么——它们逐渐转变我们认为自己是谁。

因此，培养好习惯是一种长期的自我尊重。它不关乎完美，而关乎持续、有意识的努力。五年后的你，正被你今天实践的习惯所塑造。请明智地选择它们。🌱

senior.title: 📱 The Double-Edged Sword of Social Media
senior.content:
Social media has become an inseparable part of modern life. Platforms like WeChat, Douyin, and Instagram allow people to share moments, stay connected with friends, and access information instantly. Yet this powerful tool is a double-edged sword. 📱

On the positive side, social media enables rapid communication across distances. Students can join study groups online, discuss problems, and share learning resources. During difficult times, people can receive emotional support from online communities. Businesses use these platforms to reach customers, and public organizations spread important messages quickly.

However, the negative effects are equally real. Many teenagers spend hours scrolling through short videos, which can reduce the time available for study, exercise, and face-to-face interaction. Constant comparison with others’ carefully edited lives often leads to anxiety and lower self-esteem. Addiction to likes and comments can make some people dependent on external approval rather than inner confidence.

Privacy is another serious concern. Personal information shared online may be collected and used without full awareness. Cyberbullying and the spread of false information also damage trust and mental well-being.

The key is not to abandon social media, but to use it with awareness and balance. Setting time limits, choosing high-quality content, and protecting personal information are practical steps. Offline activities—reading, sports, and real conversations—remain essential for healthy development.

Technology itself is neutral. Its value depends on how we choose to use it. By developing digital literacy and self-discipline, young people can enjoy the benefits of social media while avoiding its traps. 🌱
senior.translation:
社交媒体已成为现代生活中不可分割的一部分。微信、抖音和Instagram等平台让人们分享瞬间、与朋友保持联系、即时获取信息。然而，这个强大的工具是一把双刃剑。📱

积极方面，社交媒体使跨距离的快速沟通成为可能。学生可以加入在线学习小组、讨论问题、分享学习资源。在困难时期，人们可以从在线社区获得情感支持。企业利用这些平台接触客户，公共机构快速传播重要信息。

然而，负面影响同样真实。许多青少年花数小时刷短视频，这会减少学习、锻炼和面对面交流的时间。不断与他人精心编辑的生活比较，往往导致焦虑和自尊心下降。对点赞和评论的沉迷会让一些人依赖外部认可，而非内在自信。

隐私是另一个严重问题。在线分享的个人信息可能在不完全知情的情况下被收集和使用。网络欺凌和虚假信息的传播也会损害信任和心理健康。

关键不是放弃社交媒体，而是带着意识和平衡去使用它。设定时间限制、选择高质量内容、保护个人信息都是切实可行的步骤。线下活动——阅读、运动和真实对话——对健康发展仍然至关重要。

技术本身是中性的。它的价值取决于我们如何选择使用它。通过培养数字素养和自律，年轻人可以享受社交媒体的好处，同时避免其陷阱。🌱

senior.title: 🌍 Plastic Pollution: A Challenge We Must Face
senior.content:
Plastic is everywhere—in bottles, bags, packaging, and countless everyday products. It is cheap, light, and convenient. Yet the same qualities that make plastic useful also make it a serious environmental threat. 🌍

Most plastics do not decompose naturally for hundreds of years. When they enter rivers and oceans, they break into smaller pieces called microplastics. These tiny particles are eaten by fish and other marine animals, and eventually enter the human food chain. Birds and sea turtles often mistake plastic bags for food, which can cause injury or death.

The scale of the problem is enormous. Millions of tons of plastic waste enter the ocean every year. Beaches around the world are littered with bottles and packaging. Even remote areas far from cities are no longer free from plastic pollution.

Solving this challenge requires action at many levels. Individuals can reduce single-use plastics by carrying reusable bags and bottles. Governments can ban certain plastic products and improve recycling systems. Companies can redesign packaging and invest in alternative materials that are biodegradable or easier to recycle.

Education also plays a vital role. When people understand the long-term cost of plastic pollution, they are more likely to change their habits. Schools, media, and communities can all help raise awareness.

Plastic pollution is not someone else’s problem—it is a shared responsibility. Every choice we make, from refusing a plastic straw to supporting sustainable products, contributes to a cleaner planet. The future of our oceans and ecosystems depends on the actions we take today. 🌊
senior.translation:
塑料无处不在——瓶子、袋子、包装以及无数日常产品中。它便宜、轻便、方便。然而，让塑料有用的这些特性，也使它成为严重的环境威胁。🌍

大多数塑料在自然中数百年都不会分解。当它们进入河流和海洋时，会碎成叫做微塑料的小块。这些微小颗粒被鱼类和其他海洋动物吃掉，最终进入人类食物链。鸟类和海龟经常把塑料袋误认为食物，可能导致受伤或死亡。

问题的规模巨大。每年有数百万吨塑料废物进入海洋。世界各地的海滩上散落着瓶子和包装。即使远离城市的偏远地区也不再没有塑料污染。

解决这一挑战需要多层次的行动。个人可以通过携带可重复使用的袋子和瓶子来减少一次性塑料。政府可以禁止某些塑料产品并改善回收系统。公司可以重新设计包装，投资可生物降解或更容易回收的替代材料。

教育也起着至关重要的作用。当人们理解塑料污染的长期代价时，他们更有可能改变习惯。学校、媒体和社区都可以帮助提高意识。

塑料污染不是别人的问题——它是共同的责任。我们做出的每一个选择，从拒绝塑料吸管到支持可持续产品，都有助于更清洁的星球。我们海洋和生态系统的未来，取决于我们今天采取的行动。🌊

senior.title: 🧠 Growth Mindset: How Beliefs Shape Success
senior.content:
Have you ever thought “I’m just not good at maths” or “I’ll never be able to speak English fluently”? These thoughts reflect what psychologists call a fixed mindset—the belief that abilities are fixed and cannot change much. In contrast, a growth mindset is the belief that abilities can be developed through effort, learning, and persistence. 🧠

Research shows that students with a growth mindset tend to achieve more. When they face a difficult problem, they see it as a challenge to learn from, not as proof that they are not smart enough. They are more willing to try different strategies, ask for help, and keep practising. Students with a fixed mindset, however, often avoid challenges because failure feels like a judgment of their intelligence.

How can we develop a growth mindset? First, notice your inner voice. When you catch yourself saying “I can’t do this,” add the word “yet”—“I can’t do this yet.” This small change opens the door to future improvement. Second, value effort and strategy more than natural talent. Praise yourself and others for hard work and smart methods, not only for high scores. Third, treat mistakes as information. Every error tells you what to practise next.

Teachers and parents can also help. When feedback focuses on process—“You used a good method” or “You improved because you practised”—students learn that growth is possible. When feedback only praises results—“You’re so smart”—students may fear challenges that could threaten that label.

A growth mindset does not mean that everyone will become a genius. It means that with deliberate practice and the right strategies, most people can improve significantly in areas they care about. The belief that you can grow is itself a powerful tool for learning and life. 🌱
senior.translation:
你有没有想过“我就是不擅长数学”或“我永远无法流利说英语”？这些想法反映了心理学家所说的固定型思维——相信能力是固定的，无法有太大改变。相反，成长型思维是相信能力可以通过努力、学习和坚持得到发展。🧠

研究表明，拥有成长型思维的学生往往取得更多成就。当他们面对难题时，他们把它看作学习的挑战，而不是证明自己不够聪明。他们更愿意尝试不同策略、寻求帮助并持续练习。而固定型思维的学生常常回避挑战，因为失败感觉像是对智力的评判。

我们如何培养成长型思维？首先，注意内心的声音。当你发现自己说“我做不到”时，加上“还”——“我还做不到”。这个小改变打开了未来进步的大门。其次，更看重努力和策略，而不是天赋。表扬自己和他人的努力与聪明方法，而不只是高分。第三，把错误当作信息。每个错误都告诉你下一步该练习什么。

老师和家长也可以帮助。当反馈关注过程——“你用了好方法”或“你进步是因为练习”——学生会学到成长是可能的。当反馈只表扬结果——“你真聪明”——学生可能害怕会威胁这个标签的挑战。

成长型思维并不意味着每个人都会成为天才。它意味着通过刻意练习和正确策略，大多数人可以在自己关心的领域显著提高。相信自己可以成长，本身就是学习和生活的强大工具。🌱

questions.q: 4. What kind of feedback helps develop a growth mindset?
options: Focusing on process, effort and methods
questions.exp: When feedback focuses on process—“You used a good method”... students learn that growth is possible.

questions.q: 5. What is the main idea of the passage?
options: A growth mindset—the belief that abilities can develop—helps learning and success
questions.exp: 全文核心是成长型思维对学习与成功的作用。

senior.title: 🤝 The Value of Volunteering
senior.content:
Volunteering means offering your time and energy to help others without expecting payment. It may seem like a small act, but its impact on both the helper and the community can be profound. 🤝

For the people who receive help, volunteers can make a real difference. A student tutoring a younger child in English may improve that child’s confidence and grades. A group cleaning a park makes the neighbourhood more pleasant for everyone. During natural disasters, volunteers often provide food, shelter, and emotional support when official help is limited.

For the volunteers themselves, the benefits are equally valuable. Volunteering builds skills such as communication, teamwork, and problem-solving. It also develops empathy—the ability to understand other people’s feelings. Many students discover new interests and even future career directions through volunteer work. In addition, helping others often brings a sense of purpose and happiness that is hard to get from other activities.

Schools and communities increasingly encourage youth participation in volunteering. Some schools include community service as part of the curriculum. Online platforms make it easier to find opportunities that match personal interests, whether teaching, environmental protection, or caring for the elderly.

Of course, volunteering should be meaningful and well organized. Short, one-time actions are good, but long-term commitment often creates deeper impact. Reflection after volunteering—thinking about what was learned and what could be improved—helps turn experience into personal growth.

In a society that sometimes focuses too much on competition and individual success, volunteering reminds us of our shared responsibility. When more people choose to give a little of their time, the whole community becomes stronger and warmer. 🌱
senior.translation:
志愿服务意味着在不期望报酬的情况下，贡献时间和精力帮助他人。它看起来可能只是小行动，但对帮助者和社区的影响都可以很深远。🤝

对于接受帮助的人，志愿者可以带来真正的改变。一个学生辅导低年级孩子英语，可能提高那个孩子的自信和成绩。一个清理公园的团体让整个社区更宜人。在自然灾害中，志愿者常常在官方帮助有限时提供食物、住所和情感支持。

对志愿者自己，益处同样宝贵。志愿服务培养沟通、团队合作和解决问题等技能。它也培养同理心——理解他人感受的能力。许多学生通过志愿工作发现新兴趣甚至未来职业方向。此外，帮助他人往往带来其他活动难以获得的目标感和幸福感。

学校和社区越来越鼓励青少年参与志愿服务。一些学校把社区服务纳入课程。在线平台让寻找匹配个人兴趣的机会更容易，无论是教学、环保还是照顾老人。

当然，志愿服务应该有意义且组织良好。短期、一次性行动很好，但长期承诺往往产生更深影响。志愿服务后的反思——思考学到了什么、可以改进什么——有助于把经历转化为个人成长。

在一个有时过于关注竞争和个人成功的社会里，志愿服务提醒我们共同的责任。当更多人选择贡献一点时间时，整个社区会变得更强大、更温暖。🌱
